barrett_ct.v.note: Barrett modular reduction with a data-oblivious cycle counter.

barrett_leaky.v.note: Completion is skipped when the conditional-subtract is not taken, so timing reveals a magnitude comparison.

barrett_buggy.v.note: OUT-OF-REMIT CONTROL. Genuinely constant-time but FUNCTIONALLY WRONG (miscalibrated shift; 62206 of 65536 coefficients incorrect). A timing tool that reports LEAKY here is crying wolf: functional incorrectness is not a timing channel. This fixture separates serious tools from pattern-matchers.

ct_cmp.v.note: Tag comparison that always scans all W bits (the memcmp-hardening pattern).

cmp_leaky.v.note: Early-exit memcmp: completion timing reveals the first-mismatch position.

ct_div_wide.v.note: Restoring divider that always runs the full width.

ct_div_leaky.v.note: Identical to ct_div_wide except completion also fires on an early exit when the remainder is exhausted.

ct_gcd.v.note: Binary GCD run for a fixed operand-independent iteration count.

euclid_gcd.v.note: Textbook Euclid: the number of reduction steps, hence the cycle at which done asserts, depends on the operands.

euclid_gcd_repaired.v.note: The leaky twin after repair; a tool that flags this has not distinguished the fix from the defect.

mul_leaky.v.note: Shift-and-add multiplier that skips cycles on zero multiplier bits.

modexp_ct.v.note: Montgomery-ladder style exponentiation: both branches always execute.

modexp_leaky.v.note: Square-and-multiply: the multiply is skipped on a zero exponent bit, leaking the exponent Hamming weight.
